name: Question 20
problem:
Consider the homogeneous system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix. You're given that the standard fundamental matrix ${Φ}_{0}(t)$ is the unique solution to the initial value problem

$$
{Φ}_{0}^{′}(t)=A{Φ}_{0}(t),\,{Φ}_{0}(0)={I}_{n}.
$$

A derivation of the formula for the solution $x(t)$ passing through $x({t}_{0})$ is presented below. 

$\text{L1}:\,$ Let ${Φ}_{0}(t)={e}^{At}$

$\text{L2}:\,$ $x(t)={Φ}_{0}(t)\,c$ for some constant vector $c$

$\text{L3}:\,$ $x(t)={e}^{At}\,c$ 

$\text{L4}:\,$ $x({t}_{0})={e}^{A{t}_{0}}\,c$

$\text{L5}:\,$ $({e}^{A{t}_{0}})^{-1}x({t}_{0})=({e}^{A{t}_{0}})^{-1}{e}^{A{t}_{0}}\,c$

$\text{L6}:\,$ $c={e}^{-A{t}_{0}}x({t}_{0})\,$

$\text{L7}:\,$ $x(t)={e}^{At}{e}^{-A{t}_{0}}x({t}_{0})\,$

$\text{L8}:\,$ $x(t)={e}^{At-A{t}_{0}}x({t}_{0})\,$

$\text{L9}:\,$ $x(t)={e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}x({t}_{0})\,$

Select the correct options to justify each step of the reasoning.

$\,$ Line $\text{L6}$ follows from $\text{L5}$ by the fact that {{field-1}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L7}$ can be obtained by {{field-2}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L9}$ follows from $\text{L8}$ by the fact that {{field-3}}.

Consider the homogeneous system x′(t)=Ax(t), where A is a constant square matrix. You're given that the standard fundamental matrix Φ0(t) is the unique solution to the initial value problem Φ0′(t)=AΦ0(t),Φ0(0)=In.

A derivation of the formula for the solution x(t) passing through x(t0) is presented below.

L1: Let Φ0(t)=eAt

L2: x(t)=Φ0(t)c for some constant vector c

L3: x(t)=eAtc

L4: x(t0)=eAt0c

L5: (eAt0)−1x(t0)=(eAt0)−1eAt0c

L6: c=e−At0x(t0)

L7: x(t)=eAte−At0x(t0)

L8: x(t)=eAt−At0x(t0)

L9: x(t)=eA(t−t0)x(t0)

Select the correct options to justify each step of the reasoning.

Line L6 follows from L5 by the fact that
 
eAt0e−At0=Ie−At0
(eAt0)−1eAt0=eAt0I
(eAt0)−1=e−At0
.

Line L7 can be obtained by
 
left-multiplying x(t)=eAtc by e−At
evaluating x(t)=eAtc at t=0 and solving for c
substituting c=e−At0x(t0) into x(t)=eAtc
.

Line L9 follows from L8 by the fact that
 
eX+Y=eXeY when X and Y commute
At−At0=A(t−t0) for any t and t0
